clue.text: Clutches Greek serpents

parts.note: GR is the standard abbreviation for Greek
asps are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: Someone clutches a bunch of snakes from Greek myth, perhaps Medusa's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: "Clutches" reads as a noun in the surface, but here it is the verb: grasps.
explanation.definitionFit: To clutch something is to grasp it.

clue.text: Whingers roasted composer

indicators.note: roasting cooks and transforms, so the letters of WHINGERS come out changed

parts.note: the fodder, taken as printed

explanation.surface: Complainers gave a composer a harsh roasting.
explanation.walkthrough: "Roasted" looks like harsh criticism from the whingers; it is the cooking that rearranges them. A whinger is British slang for a moaner.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gershwin was the American composer of Rhapsody in Blue.

clue.text: After a year, one has a rest: a Cypriot resort

parts.note: taken as printed
Y is the abbreviation for year
Roman numeral one
a nap is a rest
taken as printed

explanation.surface: After a year's work, someone takes a well-earned break at a Cyprus holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces simply follow one another: after A Y comes I, which 'has' A NAP, then the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayia Napa is a party resort on the south-east coast of Cyprus.

clue.text: Fear depression's bad habits

indicators.note: the letters are in a bad state, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, including the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Someone worries that depression leads to bad habits.
explanation.walkthrough: "Habits" looks like behaviour patterns; it means garments, as in a nun's habit or riding habit. A pinafore dress is a sleeveless dress worn over a blouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a type of dress, so pinafore dresses are habits.

clue.text: Sailor's assistant we're told brings on cargo of bitumen

indicators.note: something we are told is heard, not read

parts.note: brings on cargo = loads; bitumen = tar

explanation.surface: A deckhand is said to help by loading barrels of pitch onto the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The assistant is not a person: it is the star a sailor steers by.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestar, usually the Pole Star, guides navigators at sea.

clue.text: Cockney detective's measured resistance

indicators.note: a Cockney drops the H, so Holmes is said as 'Olmes

parts.note: the detective is Sherlock Holmes

explanation.surface: A London detective takes careful stock of the opposition he faces.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class London accent, famous for dropping the H at the start of words; the L of Holmes is silent anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit stands for the quantity: a resistance, once measured, is stated as so many of these units.

clue.text: Train with Dutch boarders losing time before El Salvador? They're not certain

parts.note: to train is to educate
D is the abbreviation for Dutch
boarders are paying guests
T is the abbreviation for time
ES is El Salvador's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: A train carrying Dutch passengers runs late on its way to El Salvador, leaving everyone unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: "Train" looks like a railway train but is the verb. GUESTS minus T leaves GUESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive paraphrase: estimates made from knowledge rather than proof by nature fall short of certainty.

clue.text: Tense hold-up, I believe

definitions.note: a phrase the answer would say, standing for the noun

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a hold-up is a robbery

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a tense robbery is under way.
explanation.walkthrough: "Tense" is an adjective in the surface but the grammar noun here, giving T.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is one who says 'I believe' in God.

clue.text: Monarch and kin greatly amuse soldiers (when sent up)

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending letters up turns them around

parts.note: to slay an audience is to amuse it greatly
OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: The royal family are mocked and entertain the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: "Sent up" suggests mockery, which fits the surface; in a down answer it reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain collective: the royal family taken as a group, the sovereign plus relatives.

clue.text: Holds sway: good to assume means of control

parts.note: reins control a horse
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone who holds power ought to take the reins of control.
explanation.walkthrough: The G goes inside REINS, between I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a monarch on the throne rules, which is holding sway.

clue.text: Everyman's entirely in vulgar fashion

parts.note: the setter, Everyman, refers to himself: I am = I'M
purely means wholly

explanation.surface: The setter owns up to being thoroughly crude.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's name with 's usually means 'the setter is': I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Impurely means in a vulgar or unclean manner.

clue.text: Crusty loaf? That's a mistake

definitions.meaning: a large British loaf with a crisp crust and diagonal slashes
a silly blunder, in informal British English

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark asks you to take "Crusty loaf" as a thing, then "a mistake" gives the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is both a British loaf with diagonal slashes and a silly blunder.

clue.text: Nuisances in small numbers

explanation.surface: Pests that come only a few at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: "in" simply joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A handful is both a troublesome person and a small quantity.

clue.text: Some señoritas selected dangling ornamentation

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used

parts.note: the last three letters of the first word and the first three of the second

explanation.surface: Chosen Spanish girls wear dangling trimmings on their dresses.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tassel is a dangling tuft used as decoration.

clue.text: Bass and violin initially introducing song in a state

indicators.note: the initials come first, introducing what follows
the first letters of bass, and, violin

parts.note: first letters of each word
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: Bass and violin open an orchestral song performance, with everyone in a state of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: "initially" applies to 'and' as well as the two instruments, so AND gives its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the German region around Munich is one of that country's federal states.

clue.text: Predominates, bizarrely, having taken off

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a bizarre new way

parts.note: the fodder, taken as printed

explanation.surface: Something takes over, oddly, after taking off like a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: "Taken off" looks like departure or removal; here it means mimicked.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to impersonate them.

clue.text: Captain Charles twice briefly showing security measures

parts.note: Capt is the short form of captain
Chas is the short form of Charles
surface padding telling you both names are shortened; it adds no letters

explanation.surface: Captain Charles is shown twice in brief, as if by a security camera.
explanation.walkthrough: "twice briefly" means both names are abbreviated: Capt and Chas.
explanation.definitionFit: CAPTCHAs are website tests that keep bots out.

clue.text: Support commercial possibility

parts.note: a commercial is an advert
an option is a possibility

explanation.surface: Backing for a promising business opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: "commercial" looks like an adjective but is the noun, a TV advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption of a cause or policy is taking it up and supporting it.

clue.text: Arrangement of Elgar — and 'Land…' is what'll get your heart racing

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks the material, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as printed

explanation.surface: An arrangement of Elgar's Land of Hope and Glory is stirring enough to quicken the pulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land of Hope and Glory' is Elgar's rousing patriotic anthem, so 'Arrangement' reads as music.
explanation.definitionFit: The adrenal glands release adrenaline, which makes the heart race.

clue.text: Part of nightclub is hoppin', man!

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the phrase that follows

parts.note: the last letter of nightclub, all of is, and the first three letters of hoppin'

explanation.surface: An excited clubber shouts that the club is lively.
explanation.walkthrough: "man!" looks like an exclamation; it is a chess piece, one of the men on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces are called men, and the bishop is one of them.

clue.text: Once again evaluate a comment

definitions.meaning: to mark a piece of work a second time

explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-MARK, the first half is a teacher grading work a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-mark is to grade again; a remark is something said.

clue.text: One finding bees surrounding 10 goats

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the bees go around the ten

parts.note: taken as printed
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A beekeeper finds bees swarming round ten goats.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 looks like a cross-reference to 10 Across, but it is just the number ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the ibex is a wild mountain goat of the Alps, with long curved horns.

clue.text: Avoid sun, despite being prepared

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun

indicators.note: prepared material has been worked into a new form

parts.note: the fodder, taken as printed

explanation.surface: Someone stays out of the sun even though they have sunscreen on.
explanation.walkthrough: "despite" reads as a connecting word in the surface; it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stepping to one side dodges a blow or an awkward question.

clue.text: Shakespeare's river's rising: a stellar sight

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: Shakespeare was the Bard of Avon, from Stratford-upon-Avon

explanation.surface: The River Avon floods, and it's a spectacular sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Avon is the river through Stratford, Shakespeare's birthplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares brightly.

clue.text: Those easily angered exchanging words in a posed photograph

indicators.note: HOT and HEADS trade places, so the front three letters move to the back

parts.note: hotheads lose their temper easily

explanation.surface: Short-tempered people trade insults while posing for a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: "exchanging words" looks like an argument, but it means swapping HOT and HEADS.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: actors and professionals pose for a close portrait of the face.

clue.text: Incredibly slender terrains helping mainlands interconnect, primarily?

definitions.text: Incredibly slender terrains helping mainlands interconnect

indicators.note: the primary, first, letters of each word

parts.words: Incredibly slender terrains helping mainlands interconnect
parts.note: first letters of the six words

explanation.surface: Narrow strips of land that link continents.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Isthmi, plural of isthmus, are narrow land strips joining two larger land masses.

clue.text: Baked spanakopita OAP strangely rejected in Commonwealth country

indicators.note: O, A, P are thrown out from scattered places in the word

parts.note: taken as printed
the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A pensioner turns down a Greek spinach pie when abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAP is a British old-age pensioner. Remove O, A and P from SPANAKOPITA, then rearrange SPANKITA.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the South Asian nation is one of the Commonwealth's member states.

clue.text: Welcomes a fleece to clothe son

parts.note: taken as printed

indicators.note: the fleece wraps round the son like clothing

parts.note: a fleece is a sheep's skin
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent greets their boy with a fleece jacket to keep him warm.
explanation.walkthrough: "fleece" suggests a jacket; it is a sheepskin.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask someone in is to welcome them into your home.
